inferences.statement: Checkout's current failures are mainly payment rejections relayed upward, since the failing spans in sampled traces are payment Charge and checkout's client Charge.
Kafka is unlikely to be the cause: its revision is unchanged and it has no events.
A deployment change does not explain the 19:42 alert. The likely triggers are the flag state or a runtime dependency, not a rollout.

root_causes.cause: Checkout is the alerted service and is failing about 32% of requests. Its Charge and PlaceOrder errors are relayed payment rejections. Its earlier CurrencyService/Convert client errors from 19:24Z are unexplained and not seen in currency's server metrics, so checkout's own path or the checkout-to-currency link is a possible second contributor.

Payment rejects Charge calls with 'Invalid token' for gold-tier users, starting 19:39Z. The paymentFailure flag at 50% is the likely trigger, since it is the only non-default setting and matches the roughly half-failure pattern. Payment is the source of checkout's Charge failures but not of checkout's earlier onset.

diagnosis.summary: checkout (the alerted service) is failing about 32% of requests. Most of the current failure is payment's Charge calls being rejected with 'Invalid token' for gold-tier users, relayed through checkout, frontend and frontend-proxy. The paymentFailure flag is ON at 50%, which is the only non-default flag and the likeliest trigger, but its turn-on time is unchecked. Checkout's error burn began at 19:24Z, about 16 minutes before payment's first errors, and its CurrencyService/Convert errors are not visible on currency's side. So the onset is not explained by payment alone. No deployment changed in the window, so this is not a rollout.

alternatives.why_not: No checkout or payment rollout happened in the window; each has a single revision from 19:11Z, so there is no bad release to revert.

Payment's failures are caused by the flag state and deterministic for gold users, so a restart would not change them. A restart of checkout would not fix its unexplained earlier currency-path errors and no stuck-process evidence exists.
The failures are rejections (Invalid token) and not capacity or latency saturation, so more replicas would not reduce the error ratio.

plan.no_action_reason: The fix is to turn off the paymentFailure flag in flagd, which none of the available actions can do. A human should verify the flag change time against payment's 19:39Z onset, then check checkout-to-currency connectivity or client timeouts for the 19:24Z onset.
plan.summary: No automated action is proposed. The likely cause is the paymentFailure flag at 50% in flagd, which is outside the three actions available here. root_causes.cause: Payment is rejecting about 30-36% of Charge requests with an injected-looking 'Invalid token' failure, most likely driven by the paymentFailure flag served from flagd and enabled at 50%. Errors are fast, not timeouts, and not caused by a payment rollout.
Contributing only: flagd serves paymentFailure as ON at 50% with targeting false. This is the configuration that appears to drive payment's errors. It shows no error logs and is not itself failing.
